messages.author: 206c95168ffdfa45
messages.subject: Running ADVI in parallel (RStan)
parts:
I noticed from previous posts and personal experience that the ADVI (variational bayes) function can sometimes get stuck on local optima, so that it makes sense to try multiple runs with different random initializations, ideally in parallel. I have a few suggestions for updates to Stan (specifically, RStan which is what I use) that would facilitate this:

1. Allow a parameter analogous to "chains" that will allow multiple ADVI instances to run in parallel.
2. Expose the final value of the ELBO in the stanfit object result for each ADVI run (not just printing). Then if one ran multiple VB procedures, he/she could choose the best one based on comparing ELBO values. Note this is not model comparison but just a way of getting closer to the global optimum for a single model.
3. Allow "silent mode" to prevent so much output being printed. In parallel it would become jumbled.

The way I am currently doing parallel ADVI is:
1. Wrap calls to vb() with parallel::mclapply() to parallelize
2. Redirect STDOUT for each ADVI instance to a string using capture.output()
3. Parse the strings to get the final ELBO values and use to choose the stanfit object based on highest ELBO among the parallel instances

I can post this as an issue to github but wanted to get some feedback here first.

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Running ADVI in parallel (RStan)
parts:
Hi Will, 

We've had discussions about diagnostics involving multiple ADVI runs but, as far as I know, there hasn't been too much progress made on that yet. But I do think it's a good idea to allow running in parallel, so you could definitely open an issue on github about that. 

Jonah

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Running ADVI in parallel (RStan)
parts:
I believe ADVI should be set up to simulate from the approximate
posterior and return a result in the same form as MCMC. You
can use R-hat on that to evaluate whether or not the multiple
runs of ADVI hit the same posterior.

- Bob
